title: Reflecting a Graph Across the x-Axis: y = -f(x)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given the graph of y=f(x), describe precisely how the graph of y=-f(x) is obtained and what happens to a typical point (a,b) on the original curve.

steps.title: Interpret the Formula
steps.explanation: At every input x the new output is the negative of the old output; inputs are untouched.
steps.why: Negation is applied to the whole function value, which is a vertical operation.

steps.title: Track a Typical Point
steps.explanation: A point at height b above the axis moves to depth b below it, keeping the same x-coordinate.
steps.why: Vertical flip about the horizontal axis preserves abscissas and reverses signs of ordinates.

steps.title: Describe the Sketch
steps.explanation: The new curve is the mirror image of the old one seen in the x-axis: parts above dip below and vice versa; points where f=0 stay put.
steps.why: Fixed points of the transformation are exactly the x-intercepts of f.

steps.title: Summarize the Rule
steps.explanation: Every point of y=f(x) is reflected straight across the x-axis, producing y=-f(x).
steps.why: This is the standard vertical reflection transformation.
